subject: Quick follow-up — security packet & any review blockers for Acme Cloud
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & security packet — Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — great to meet you and the Acme Cloud team today. Quick recap from our discovery call:

- Use case: low-latency inference for multi-tenant analytics (primarily us-west users)
- Expected Q3 pilot: ~50k tokens/day, scaling to 500k in 6 months
- Primary concerns: data isolation, auditability, and incident response SLAs

Per our agreement on the call, I attached the Redwood security packet (redwood_security_packet_v2.pdf) and a network diagram for your infra team. Key items inside: SOC 2 summary, encryption/KMS options, private deployment checklist, and our standard data retention defaults. I also uploaded the packet here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/AcmeCloud/redwood_security_packet_v2

Next steps I propose:
1) Your security team reviews the packet — any blocking questions flagged back to us
2) If helpful, we schedule a 30-minute technical QA with our security engineer (Lauren) to walk through scope and clarifications
3) Parallel: I'll prepare a simple mutual action plan (MAP) with target dates for the pilot

Are there any blockers we should know about or a preferred time window for a short QA call next week?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood_security_packet_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)
Attachment: redwood_network_diagram.png (image/png, 160KB)
From: Sara Li <sara@acmecloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Security <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & security packet — Redwood Inference

Hi Marcus — thanks for the packet and the clear recap. I've shared it with our security and infra leads; they plan to do an initial pass during PI planning next week.

I'll loop back if they have high-level blockers, otherwise expect a follow-up by the end of week after the review. If it's helpful, put some times next Tue/Wed afternoon and I can ask our security lead to join.

Best,
Sara
Head of Platform | Acme Cloud
(sara@acmecloud.com)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Circling back — any blockers on the security packet?

Hi Sara — checking in since I haven't heard back after your note. Quick list of options from our side if your security reviewers surface anything:

- We can provide an abbreviated SOC 2 scoping memo that covers only the pilot systems (fast turn: 3 business days)
- Offer a live 30-minute session with our security/infra lead to answer questions and walk the network diagram
- Provide a short JIRA-style checklist your team can use to sign off the pilot dependencies

If none of these are blockers and the review is simply queued, no problem — would you mind letting me know the rough timing? Also, if you have procurement questions (T&Cs, POC pricing), we can start a parallel thread so it doesn't delay the security review.

Suggested slots (PT): Wed 6/9 2:00–2:30pm, Thu 6/10 11:00–11:30am, Fri 6/11 3:00–3:30pm. Happy to adjust to your team's availability.

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick note — narrow scoping & offer to join security review call

Hi Sara — Lauren from Redwood on the security/SE side. Re-forwarding Marcus's note below. If your reviewers want a tighter deliverable, we can produce a narrow scoping memo (one page) that documents which systems are in-scope for the pilot and the controls we rely on. That usually speeds internal approvals.

If useful, I can join a 20–30 minute call with your security lead and run through:
- the SOC-adjacent controls we rely on (encryption, key rotation, RBAC)
- our private deployment options and required networking (VPN/VPC peering)
- evidence we can share (audit summaries, runbooks)

Let me know if you have a preferred time next week; otherwise, Marcus, we can book one of the slots you suggested.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
